collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult aged 30 or older and another adult)

collection.description: A villager laughs at how scared they were before their first day of work: tell a friend, or wonder what they will laugh at later.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has just remembered, for no reason, how terrified (subject.he/she) was before (subject.his/her) first day of real work with the adults. (subject.He/she) didn't sleep for two nights. (subject.He/she) was sure (subject.he/she) would do everything wrong and everyone would laugh. (subject.He/she) can't even remember what happened on the actual day. Nothing, probably.

choices.label: Wonder What You'll Laugh at Later

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) wonders what (subject.he/she) is worrying about now that (subject.he/she) will laugh at in twenty years. (subject.He/she) can think of three things right away. (subject.He/she) tries laughing at them now, to save time. It doesn't quite work. But it makes them a little smaller. (subject.He/she) decides that's progress.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (subject) tells (friend), laughing. (friend) laughs too, then admits (friend.he/she) was exactly the same: (friend.he/she) was so scared before (friend.his/her) first day that (friend.he/she) hid in a tree. "Did they find you?" "Eventually. I'd fallen asleep." They spend the evening trading things they used to be terrified of. Most of them are very silly now. A few still aren't.
